transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hello. I guess I'm here because... well, I just have a hard time staying in my chair. 

At staff meetings, or even just sitting at dinner... I always end up getting up when everyone else is still seated. I'll, um, suddenly go refill my coffee, or walk to the back of the room to check a handout. Things like that. Even when nothing is really urgent. So... that's mainly it.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around even when you're not in meetings or sitting down for meals?

I suppose so. Um... since the house got quieter—my youngest left for college a bit ago—I just... keep going. I'll go from lesson planning to starting laundry, then out to softball practice, and then maybe chopping food for a community event. I just move from one thing to the next without much pause. Even on nights I told myself I'd just rest. I just... don't really stop.
Do you often feel impatient or have trouble waiting your turn in situations like lines, conversations, or while waiting for your food at a restaurant?

Um... not really, no. I mean, waiting in line is just... waiting in line. I don't think I'm particularly impatient. I just wait like everyone else, I guess. I haven't really noticed any issues with that.
Do you often feel like you need to be doing something active, even when you're not necessarily busy or pressured to get things done?
Um... I don't know. I guess I'm just used to keeping busy. I don't really think about it as needing to be active, exactly. I just... do what needs doing, I suppose.
Do you find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat when you're expected to stay still for a while, like during a meeting or watching a movie?

I suppose I do a bit of that. Um... when I'm at my desk grading essays, or... or sitting in church, I'll realize I'm tapping my foot. Or clicking my pen. Sometimes I shift around a lot and just have to... tell myself to settle down. But I think that's normal.
Do you find yourself talking more than usual, or feeling like you can't stop talking even when you're not particularly excited or trying to contribute?

Um... maybe a little. I wouldn't say I can't stop, but... I suppose I can take over a conversation sometimes. Just... at work, in the Spanish department, or at the cultural center. 

I might... well, I tend to give three examples when one would probably do. And then I'll see people trying to wrap it up, and... it's a bit embarrassing. But I don't really mean to do it. I just like to be thorough, I guess.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep or not feeling tired even when you haven't slept much?
Um... no, not really. I think I sleep about the same as I always have. If I only get a few hours, I... I definitely feel tired the next day. So, no, nothing like that.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing, or that you're jumping from one idea to another so quickly that it's hard to keep up?
Um... no, not really. I don't think my thoughts race. I just... think about my day, or my lesson plans, like anyone else would. I can keep track of things fine. So, no.
Do you ever feel that your level of activity or restlessness causes you distress or interferes with your work, relationships, or other important parts of your life?

I suppose... yes. It does affect things a bit. Just... at work, in our meetings, and at my book club. People seem to lose patience with me. I go hoping to connect with everyone, and... well, I just leave feeling embarrassed instead. So... yes.
Do you ever feel an inner sense of agitation or discomfort when you're not moving, like you physically can't sit still even if you want to?

Um... no, not really. I don't think I feel... agitated. I mean, I prefer to keep busy, but it's not like I'm uncomfortable if I'm not moving. I just... I like having things to do. But no, I don't feel that kind of inner discomfort you're talking about.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or activities, like losing track of what you're doing, getting easily distracted, or forgetting what you were supposed to do next?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I can focus on my lessons just fine. I don't really lose track of what I'm doing. I just... I get my work done. So, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that.
Can you describe any times when you moved around a lot without a clear reason, like pacing or fidgeting just because you felt like you had to move, even when there wasn’t anything to do?
I don't... no. Not really. If I'm moving around, it's because I have a reason to. I'm on my feet a lot during the day for my classes, but... I don't just pace around for nothing. So... no.
Have you ever found yourself moving around, like tapping, fidgeting, or doing small tasks, even when there’s no real purpose or goal behind it—almost like your body just needs to be in motion?

I suppose... maybe a little bit. Just small things. Like if I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or... in church. I guess I'll catch myself tapping my foot, or clicking my pen. Just shifting around in my seat. Sometimes I do have to... remind myself to just settle down. But that's about it.
Can you tell me more about how your restlessness and activity affect your ability to function in your job, social life, or other important areas of your life?

I suppose... well. It's mostly just... in staff meetings. At school. Or, um, my book club. I've noticed people... they seem to lose patience with me sometimes. It's starting to affect my relationships with them, I guess. I usually just leave those things feeling... rather embarrassed, really. Instead of feeling connected to anyone. But... yes, that's about it.

Do you notice this restlessness or tendency to keep moving mostly in certain situations, like at work or in meetings, or does it happen in other places too—like at home, in social settings, or when you're alone?

Well... I suppose it happens at home, too. The house is a bit quieter now, since my youngest left for college. So I just... I keep busy, I guess. I'll go straight from lesson planning to doing a load of laundry, or... I'll be at softball practice, and then I'm chopping food for a community event. I don't really pause much. Even on the nights I promise myself I'm just going to rest... I usually end up just moving from one thing to the next.

Have you ever had difficulty completing tasks or responsibilities because you were too restless or impulsive, such as interrupting others, taking over conversations, or starting new tasks before finishing old ones?

Well... maybe just the interrupting part. I don't really know about the rest. But... in group discussions, like at our curriculum meetings, or that book club I mentioned. I suppose I do tend to jump in before someone has quite finished their thought. It's just... the response is already in my head, and I... I end up blurting it out before I can really stop myself. But... that's mostly it.
Can you tell me if your restlessness or tendency to keep moving happens in most areas of your life, like at home, at work, and in social settings, or if it's mainly in certain places or situations?

I... well, I thought I just mentioned that, really. It happens at school, and at home... and at my book club, like I said. So... yes, I guess it's just in most areas of my life. I haven't really paid much attention to it beyond that, to be honest. It's just... everywhere, I suppose.
